Stated Claim / Post Context:
Husband, 45, is charged with murder after GP 'for the Royal Family' is found dead 'while hosting sleepover' at her home near Sandringham estate

Hannah Cain, who worked as a GP, was found dead aged 45 at her house in Dersingham, Norfolk, during the early hours of Sunday morning.

Actual Article Body:
By GETHIN HICKS, REPORTER and ANDREW LEVY, REPORTER

Published:  05:18 AEST, 7 October 2026   |  Updated:  19:36 AEST, 7 October 2026

A man has been charged with murdering his GP wife after she was found dead at her home near the Sandringham estate.

Hannah Cain, 45, who is understood to have worked with the Royal Family, was found dead in the early hours of Sunday in Dersingham, Norfolk.

She had apparently been hosting a children’s sleepover at the time.

Her husband Mark Cain was subsequently arrested and was on Tuesday charged with her murder, the Crown Prosecution Service confirmed yesterday evening.

He has been remanded into custody and will appear at Norwich Magistrates' Court for an initial hearing on Wednesday morning.

Ms Cain had worked with the Royal Family, and treated senior members like Queen Camilla.

The King and Queen are understood to have been informed of her death.

The surgery in nearby Grimston where Ms Cain worked was closed on Monday. Colleagues at Grimston Medical Centre said it was due to 'extremely difficult circumstances affecting our practice team'.

Known professionally as Dr Hannah Terry, she also worked for the cosmetic treatments business Norfolk Sky Aesthetics.

Hannah Cain was found dead aged 45 at her house in Dersingham, Norfolk, during the early hours of Sunday

Ms Cain, who worked as a GP, was said to have been hosting a sleepover when she was found dead

Her husband Mark Cain, right, 45, has now been charged with her murder, the Crown Prosecution Service confirmed

Michael Devaney, Senior Crown Prosecutor, said: 'The Crown Prosecution Service has decided to prosecute Mark Cain, 45, with the murder of Dr Hannah Cain.

'It follows an investigation by Norfolk Police at her home in Dersingham.'

A surgery spokesman said on social media: 'We are sorry to let patients know that Grimston Medical Centre, including the dispensary, is temporarily closed due to extremely difficult circumstances affecting our practice team.

'We apologise for the disruption and appreciate your patience and understanding at what is a very difficult time for our colleagues.'

Bouquets and tributes were left at the scene in the hours after Ms Cain's death as forensics teams and police officers began their probe.

Villagers described the area as a normally peaceful spot and said they had been shocked by the tragedy.

One, who described how Ms Cain had lived in the area for around ten years, said: 'She was just a lovely human being with three gorgeous young children.'

A neighbour in his 90s added: 'I very rarely saw them. The children were lovely, two boys and a younger girl.

'They used to kick their football into my garden and I'd throw it back to them, or they'd come and ask me if they could come in and look for it.'

Another man who has lived in the area for half a century said there was little crime there.

'Dersingham might not have a centre but it's got a heart,' he said.

Another resident said: 'It's the sort of place where if you forget to lock your car and leave it out all night nothing will happen to it.'

One mourner meanwhile posted on Facebook: 'Fly high and sleep well Dr Terry. You never deserved this to happen, heaven has gained an angel.

'You were a lovely doctor who listened to us and helped us. Thinking of you and your family and your children and friends.'

Ms Cain was found dead at her home near the Sandringham estate and is said to have been a GP for the Royal Family

East Anglia forensic teams investigate the scene in Dersingham on Monday

'He was arrested after a woman’s body was found at an address in Fern Hill in the early hours of Sunday, October 4.

'Subject to confirmation at formal inquest proceedings the woman has been identified as 45-year-old Hannah Cain.
